points.text: Around the Mediterranean the dry summer can last from June to October, with almost no rain.
Hot, dry and windy weather lets fires start, grow and spread more easily.
Fire usually moves faster uphill, and wind feeds it oxygen and pushes it toward new fuel.

prevention.text: If you see smoke in a forest or field, keep your distance and call 112 right away.
At harvest time, sparks from harvesting machines can start fires, so machine maintenance matters.

points.text: Some fires are too small or not hot enough for a satellite to notice, so quiet weeks on the calendar can still contain small burns.
A satellite hot spot is not always a vegetation fire. It can also be a volcano or a gas flare, which is why static industrial sources are filtered out here.

stubble.title: Agricultural burning season
stubble.text: Burning crop stubble damages soil life and organic matter, leaves soil open to erosion, and its smoke can reduce visibility on roads. Stubble burning is banned in Türkiye and violations are penalised.
stubble.source_name: Şanlıurfa Provincial Directorate of Agriculture and Forestry

caveat.text: No detection does not mean no fire: clouds, thick smoke or tree canopy can hide a fire, and a fire can start and end between two overpasses.
